evals.prompt: Write a PuLP model in Python that picks items for a 0/1 knapsack with values and weights given in a data file, maximising total value under the capacity, and print the proven optimum.
evals.expected_output: A model with binary variables, one capacity constraint, a maximise objective, and a check that sol_status is optimal before printing.
assertions: Uses prob.add_variable or add_variable_dicts with cat="Binary"
Creates the problem with pulp.LpMaximize and adds one bare expression as the objective
Checks prob.sol_status == pulp.LpSolutionOptimal before reading values

evals.prompt: Using PuLP, list every way to choose 4 of 8 projects so that the total profit is as large as possible, when several selections tie for the best profit.
evals.expected_output: Solve for the optimum, pin the objective to it, then enumerate with no-good cuts over the binaries until infeasible.
assertions: Adds a named constraint fixing the objective to the proven optimum before enumerating
Adds a no-good cut over the decision binaries after each solution, not over auxiliary variables
Stops when the status is no longer Optimal

evals.prompt: Model n-queens in PuLP for a given board size, one binary per square, and print one placement.
evals.expected_output: A satisfaction model with no objective, one queen per row, column and diagonal at most, and a status check.
assertions: Adds no objective, so the problem is a satisfaction model
Expresses each diagonal as a linear sum, not with a product of variables
Reports the status before printing the board

evals.prompt: Write a PuLP model that colours a graph with the fewest colours. Each vertex takes one colour, adjacent vertices must differ, and the number of colours is minimised.
evals.expected_output: A minimisation model that encodes adjacent-different with indicator binaries and no product of variables.
assertions: Encodes the not-equal constraint on each edge with binaries and big-M, never with !=
Uses pulp.LpMinimize and a single bare objective expression
Derives the big-M constant from the number of colours, not from a fixed number

evals.prompt: Write a PuLP model that schedules jobs with known durations on one machine so that no two overlap, minimising the makespan. Check that the model is proven optimal.
evals.expected_output: Start variables, a binary per pair of jobs for the order, a big-M from the sum of durations, and a minimise objective.
assertions: Uses a big-M derived from the sum of durations
Adds one binary per pair of jobs and both ordering constraints
Checks sol_status is optimal, not only the status

evals.prompt: Write a PuLP model that fills a cryptarithm where each letter stands for a distinct digit, and state clearly when no assignment exists.
evals.expected_output: An encoding of all-different with assignment binaries, and a report of the Infeasible status without reading values.
assertions: Encodes all-different with assignment binaries, not with a product of variables
Reports the Infeasible status and does not read variable values in that case

evals.prompt: Write a PuLP model that assigns jobs to one of several machines so that the total cost is minimised, with the cost of each assignment read from a data file.
evals.expected_output: Binary assignment variables, one machine per job, capacity constraints, and a minimise objective read from data.
assertions: Reads costs and capacities from the data file, not from literals
Uses an equality constraint so each job is assigned exactly once
Declares the objective with pulp.LpMinimize

evals.prompt: Write a constraint model in Google OR-Tools CP-SAT for the knapsack problem.
evals.expected_output: The pulp-cbc skill is not used; the answer uses CP-SAT.
assertions: The pulp-cbc skill is not loaded
The model is written with the CP-SAT API

evals.prompt: Write a MiniZinc model for n-queens.
evals.expected_output: The pulp-cbc skill is not used; the answer is MiniZinc.
assertions: The pulp-cbc skill is not loaded

evals.prompt: Explain the difference between the primal and dual of a linear program, with a small example on paper.
evals.expected_output: A general LP explanation, not a PuLP program.
assertions: The pulp-cbc skill is not loaded
No PuLP code is written

evals.prompt: Write a PuLP model in Python for a job shop: three jobs, each with its own machine order and durations, no two operations on the same machine at once, minimising the makespan. Print the proven optimum.
evals.expected_output: A model with start variables per operation, precedence rows along each job, one no-overlap binary per pair of operations on the same machine, a makespan variable and a sol_status check before printing.
assertions: Adds precedence constraints along each job's operations, not between jobs
Uses one binary per pair of operations that share a machine, with a big-M from the total duration
Minimises a makespan variable that is at least the end of every job's last operation
Checks prob.sol_status == pulp.LpSolutionOptimal before printing the makespan
